text:
Withdrawn in the peace of these solitudes, with few but learned books together, I converse with the departed and listen with my eyes to the dead.

Though not always understood, always open, they correct or enrich my affairs; and in silent musical counterpoint they speak awake to life's sleep.

The great souls death removes, learned printing, avenger of the injuries of years, frees, O great Don Josef.

The hour flees irretrievably; but best reckons the hour that improves us through reading and study.


We thank Francisco Larrión Riveroll for suggesting this poem for the Ciudad Seva Digital Library.
